title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten scratch computation, apparently on the back of a typescript page of SGA 7 IX; the neighbouring pages are unrelated typescript. It belongs to the notes for the 1976 IHES lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex.

Setting. k is a base ring. S_k = k<T> is most likely the divided-power polynomial algebra in one variable, with basis T^{(i)} and multiplication T^{(i)}T^{(l)} = c_{i,l} T^{(i+l)}, where c_{i,l} = binom(i+l, i). For a k-module M, put M_{S_k} = M ⊗_k S_k, a graded S_k-module. tau_alpha is the truncation in degrees >= alpha; for S_k this is the divided-power ideal generated by the T^{(i)} with i >= alpha. Hom^d denotes graded S_k-linear maps of degree d.

Top of the page: a stabilization statement. For alpha, beta >= 0 and d >= beta - alpha, the map Hom^d(tau_alpha M_S, tau_beta N_S) -> Hom^d(tau_alpha' M_S, tau_beta' N_S) is an isomorphism whenever alpha' >= alpha, beta' >= beta and beta' - alpha' >= d. So the limiting Hom over ever deeper truncations exists and is reached at a finite stage.

This is the exact analogue of Serre's description of homomorphisms in the category of graded modules modulo torsion (the Proj / Serre-quotient picture), with the polynomial ring replaced by the divided-power algebra.

The stable value is then rewritten in several equivalent forms:
- Hom^d(tau_gamma M, N) for gamma >= -d when d <= 0, or Hom^d(M, tau_gamma N) when 0 <= gamma <= d;
- Hom^d(M, phi tau N);
- Hom^d(S_k, phi_0(Hom_k(M,N)_{S_k}));
- the degree-d component (phi_0(Hom_k(M,N)_{S_k}))_d.

Here phi_0 is a 'section / ideal-transform' functor: (phi_0 M_S)_d = Hom^{-d}(tau_d S_k, M_S), i.e. stable maps out of the truncated ideals. This is the analogue of Gamma_*(M~), the module of sections over the punctured spectrum.

Bottom of the page: computing phi_0 explicitly. A degree -d map u: tau_d S -> M ⊗ S is determined by u(T^{(i)}) = xi_i T^{(i-d)} for i >= d, with xi_i in M. S-linearity, tested on T^{(l)}, gives two expressions:
- u(T^{(i)}T^{(l)}) = c_{i,l} xi_{i+l} T^{(i+l-d)};
- T^{(l)} u(T^{(i)}) = c_{i-d,l} xi_i T^{(i+l-d)}.
Hence the boxed condition c_{i,l} xi_{i+l} = c_{i-d,l} xi_i for i >= d, l >= 0. In particular c_{d,l} xi_{d+l} = xi_d.

Interpretation. Over Q the binomial coefficients are invertible: S is just a polynomial ring, all xi are determined by xi_d, and phi_0 behaves like the Laurent-type ideal transform. Over Z or in characteristic p, the non-invertibility of binom(d+l, d) makes phi_0 a genuinely different object governed by p-adic divisibility of binomial coefficients. Presumably the aim is to understand Hom/Ext and duality for modules over divided-power algebras (PD de Rham / crystalline setting) via a 'Proj-type' localization of PD-graded modules.
errors: No outright error in the linearity computation: both sides are computed correctly, given T^{(i)}T^{(l)} = binom(i+l, i) T^{(i+l)}.
The written specialization c_{d,l} xi_{d+l} = xi_d uses c_{0,l} = 1, which is correct.
The stabilization claim and the ranges for gamma are stated without proof; the case split (d <= 0 versus 0 <= gamma <= d) is only partly legible and may be incomplete.
The writing T^l (instead of T^{(l)}) in the middle lines appears to be a notational slip; the coefficient c_{i,l} only makes sense for a divided power T^{(l)}.

ideas.what: Stabilization of graded Homs between truncations: Hom^d(tau_alpha M, tau_beta N) is independent of alpha, beta once beta - alpha >= d.
ideas.modern_name: Serre quotient by torsion / Hom in the 'Proj' category (colimit over truncations)
ideas.where_published: EGA II §2.7 and EGA III (graded modules modulo torsion / Gamma_* constructions), for polynomial-type graded rings

ideas.what: Section functor phi_0 defined by (phi_0 M)_d = Hom^{-d}(tau_d S, M_S) for the divided-power algebra S = k<T>.
ideas.modern_name: ideal transform / Gamma_* (local-cohomology-type functor) for divided-power polynomial algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure for the divided-power version; the general ideal transform goes back to Nagata / Grothendieck (SGA 2 local cohomology)
ideas.where_published: not in the published record as far as I know; the 1976 IHES lecture on the PD de Rham complex was not published by Grothendieck

ideas.what: Explicit description of degree -d S-linear maps from the PD ideal tau_d S into M ⊗ S: sequences xi_i satisfying binom(i+l, i) xi_{i+l} = binom(i+l-d, i-d) xi_i.
ideas.modern_name: computation of Hom over divided-power algebras (Gamma(T)-modules), dual to k[T]-module computations
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard-type computation (cf. Berthelot's crystalline cohomology, Illusie)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a Serre-type 'Proj' / ideal-transform formalism for graded modules over the divided-power polynomial algebra. He is computing the section functor phi_0, whose behaviour in characteristic p is governed by divisibility of binomial coefficients. This is presumably aimed at a duality or Hom-description for the divided-power de Rham complex. The page stops at the defining recursion; it does not solve it or state the structure of phi_0 in characteristic p.
missed.quote: (phi_0 M_{S_k})_d = Hom^{-d}(tau_d S_k, M_{S_k}) ... c_{i,l} xi_{i+l} = c_{i-d,l} xi_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A 'Proj of a divided-power algebra' / torsion-quotient theory for PD-graded modules is close to themes in modern work on derived de Rham and crystalline cohomology and on duality for PD algebras. It is mildly interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's approach in the unpublished 1976 lecture, but the computation itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary but purposeful scratch computation. It transposes Serre's graded-module/Proj formalism to divided-power polynomial algebras and derives the S-linearity recursion. It documents the method of an unpublished lecture but contains no striking result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'M_𝒢 k-module' is most likely 'M a k-module' (i.e. 'M k-module').
'M ⊗_k k{T}' is most likely the divided-power algebra k<T> (S_k), not a power series ring.
In 'u(T^{(i)} T^{ℓ})' and 'u(T^{(i)}) T^{ℓ}', T^{ℓ} should be read as T^{(ℓ)} (divided power), consistent with the coefficient c_{iℓ}.
In the third line of the right-hand chain, the left argument looks like M_{S_k} (with subscript S_k), not M_{𝒢_k}.
The crossed-out first line appears to be an abandoned condition such as 'δ ≤ ..., β ≥ 0', superseded by 'α, β ≥ 0, d ≥ β − α'.
In the parenthetical conditions under the first isomorphism, the crossed-out word could be 'exists' or 'exact'; it is illegible and abandoned, followed by 'β' − α' ≥ d'.
'(sinon Hom^d(M, τ_γ N)' reads more like 'sinon Hom^d(M, τ_γ N) si 0 ≤ γ ≤ d' (abbreviated 'si' / 'sinon'); the exact range is partly illegible.
